| AS23-609 | A fetus at risk of cyanosis after birth (examples: transposition with intact septum or ventricular septal defect, double-outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary defect, tetralogy) is followed every 4-8 weeks and late in the third trimester, assessing atrial septal excursion, foramen opening and ductal shunting, with maternal hyperoxygenation testing considered. | ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 15 (follow-up imaging for specific CHD diagnoses), p. 719 | ai-cross-checked | |
| AS23-610 | A fetus at risk of pulmonary venous obstruction after birth (examples: hypoplastic left heart with restrictive atrial septum, obstructed anomalous pulmonary venous return, cor triatriatum) is followed every 4-8 weeks and late in the third trimester, assessing the pulmonary venous forward-to-reverse ratio, atrial septal position and thickness, vertical vein Doppler, with maternal hyperoxygenation testing considered. | ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 15 (follow-up imaging for specific CHD diagnoses), p. 719 | ai-cross-checked | |
